title: Introduction
text: WhatFlow connects your Shopify store to WhatsApp through Meta's official WhatsApp Business Platform (the Cloud API). It sends the messages your store would normally send by email (order confirmations, COD checks, shipping updates, cart reminders), and it gives your team one shared inbox for the replies. These docs cover WhatFlow Business API (Shopify App Store listing). WhatFlow Chat Automation is a separate app that links a phone the way WhatsApp Web does. The two apps have different setups and settings. Compare them.

title: Install WhatFlow
text: WhatFlow is an embedded Shopify app. You install it from the Shopify App Store, then you work in it from your Shopify admin. This page covers installing the app, the Home screen, the app menu and choosing a plan.

title: Install WhatFlow
text: Go to WhatFlow Official API on the Shopify App Store and click install. Shopify shows the store data WhatFlow needs, such as orders, customers, products, draft orders and fulfillments. Approve it to finish the install. The app opens on the Home screen. You can always find it again under Apps › WhatFlow in your Shopify admin. If your session runs out while the app is open, you see a Session expired banner. Click Reload , or Re-authenticate if Shopify asks for updated permissions.

title: Install WhatFlow
text: WhatFlow needs an active subscription to send any message. Without one, nothing is sent: automations are skipped, and order-based automations tag the order WhatFlow: Subscription Required . Click Billing in the app menu, or Select a Plan in the setup guide. Click Select plan . Shopify's plan page opens. Choose a plan and approve the charge in Shopify. Back on Billing , the Subscription section shows your current plan with an Active badge. If you are on a trial, it shows when the trial ends. Every plan includes every feature. Plans differ in how many messages are included and the price of extra messages. See Plans and billing and the pricing page. Your WhatFlow plan does not include Meta's WhatsApp charges. Meta bills those to the payment method on your WhatsApp account. See Connect WhatsApp.

title: Connect WhatsApp
text: WhatFlow sends messages from your own WhatsApp business number through Meta's Cloud API. You connect the number once, with Meta's sign-up window, from the Connections page. Nothing sends until the number is connected. Connection › Connections The menu item is called Connection . The page it opens is called Connections .

title: Connect WhatsApp
text: Have these ready: - The Facebook account you use for your business. Meta's window signs you in with it. You can pick an existing Meta business portfolio and WhatsApp account, or create them during sign-up. - The phone number customers will message. It must be able to receive a verification code from Meta by SMS or call. - A computer. Meta opens a sign-in window that phones often block. If nothing opens, connect from a computer. Which number can you use - A new number , or one not yet on the WhatsApp Business Platform. This is the simplest case. - A number already on the WhatsApp Business app. Meta can connect it to the Cloud API while it stays on the app. Meta calls this coexistence. WhatFlow waits until Meta has finished that setup before it registers the number. - A number that already has a two-step verification PIN. You will be asked for the PIN. See Two-step verification PIN.

title: Connect WhatsApp
text: Click Connection in the WhatFlow menu, or Connect Account in the Home setup guide. Under Connect WhatsApp , click Connect with Facebook . Meta's sign-up window opens. In Meta's window, sign in, choose or create your business portfolio and WhatsApp Business account, add your phone number and verify it with the code Meta sends. Then close the window when Meta says you are done. If more than one Messaging account (Meta used to call this a WABA) owns the number, WhatFlow shows Finish WhatsApp setup . Pick one in Messaging account for templates and billing . Your templates and Meta charges belong to this account. WhatFlow registers the number with Meta. If the number already has a two-step verification PIN, you are asked for it in Six-digit registration PIN . Enter it and click Continue . You see "WhatsApp connected. Templates and Inbox are being prepared." The page now shows Your WhatsApp number with a Connected status. If something goes wrong part way through, click Restart signup to start again.

title: Connect WhatsApp
text: Meta protects each WhatsApp number with a six-digit two-step verification PIN. - New numbers: WhatFlow registers the number with the PIN 000000 . You don't need to do anything during sign-up. - Numbers that already have a PIN: WhatFlow asks for it. You see "This number already has a two-step verification PIN. Enter that six-digit PIN to finish." - You don't know the PIN: turn off two-step verification for the number in WhatsApp Manager, then enter 000000 . - Wrong PIN: you see "That PIN doesn't match this number's two-step verification PIN." Try again, or turn off two-step verification in WhatsApp Manager and enter 000000 . If WhatFlow registered your number with 000000 , change it to a PIN only you know. Go to Advanced › Two-step verification PIN , enter a new PIN and click Change PIN . You need this PIN if the number is ever registered again.

title: WhatsApp rules to know
text: WhatsApp is stricter than email or SMS. Meta sets these rules for every business that uses the WhatsApp Business Platform, and WhatFlow follows them. Knowing them up front explains most "why didn't this send?" questions.

title: WhatsApp rules to know
text: There are two kinds of business message: - Template messages are written in advance and approved by Meta. Every automation in WhatFlow (order confirmation, COD verification, cart reminders, shipping updates, broadcasts) sends a template, because the store is starting the conversation. - Free-form messages are ordinary replies, typed by your team in Live Inbox or sent by auto-replies. They can only be delivered while the customer's 24-hour window is open. Read more in Message templates.

title: WhatsApp rules to know
text: When a customer sends you a message, a 24-hour window opens. During that window you can reply with anything: text, images, products or buttons. Each new message from the customer restarts the 24 hours. Once the window closes, you can only message that customer with an approved template. Live Inbox shows how much time is left on each chat. When the window is closed, it shows Templates only and asks you to send an approved template to restart the conversation. Sending a template does not open the window. It opens again when the customer replies. A customer who taps a button in one of your templates, such as Confirm Order , sends you a message. That opens a new 24-hour window, so your team can follow up in Live Inbox for free-form replies.

title: WhatsApp rules to know
text: Meta puts every template in one of three categories, and charges by category. You choose the category when you create a template in WhatFlow. Category Used for WhatFlow templates for Utility Updates about an order the customer placed. Order confirmation and COD confirmation, order notification, order paid, cancellation, fulfillment, shipping updates, draft order invoices, review requests from the library Marketing Promotions, offers and reminders. Customers must be able to opt out. Broadcasts, abandoned checkout reminders, back in stock Authentication One-time passcodes. WhatsApp writes the text. OTP verification (only Authentication templates work there) Meta decides the final category during review. If a utility template contains promotional wording, Meta may approve it as marketing instead, and it will be charged at the marketing rate. Once a template is approved, its category can't be changed in WhatFlow. Create a new template instead. The category also matters for the Blocklist. When the blocklist is on, it can block marketing templates only, or marketing and utility templates. Authentication codes are never blocked.

title: WhatsApp rules to know
text: Meta requires that a customer has agreed to receive WhatsApp messages from your business before you message them. Collecting that consent is your job: - WhatFlow does not check Shopify marketing consent. Automations and broadcasts are sent to the phone number on the order or customer, whether or not the customer ticked a marketing box in Shopify. - WhatFlow has no opt-in checkbox for checkout. Collect consent in your own checkout, forms or policies. - Opt-outs are handled by the Blocklist. When a customer sends STOP, WhatFlow records the opt-out. But Respect blocklist is off by default, so automated messages keep going to that customer until you turn it on. Turn on Respect blocklist before you send marketing messages. Messaging people who haven't agreed to hear from you can lower your number's quality rating and messaging limits. Marketing messages need extra care. Meta does not guarantee delivery of marketing templates, and may not deliver some of them even when everything on your side is correct. A customer can also stop marketing messages from businesses inside WhatsApp. Those messages fail with the order tag WhatsApp: Opted Out .

title: WhatsApp rules to know
text: Meta gives every WhatsApp number a quality rating (green, yellow or red) based on how customers react to your messages. Blocks and reports lower it. Meta also rates each template, and WhatFlow pauses automations whose template is rated red. Each number also has a messaging limit : how many different customers you can start conversations with in a rolling 24 hours. Meta sets and raises this limit. You can see both on the Connections page under Advanced . To keep quality high: - Message people who asked to hear from you. - Keep marketing messages relevant and not too frequent. - Make it easy to opt out, and turn on Respect blocklist so opt-outs take effect straight away. If Meta restricts your account, WhatFlow turns off all automations. You need to turn them back on after Meta lifts the restriction. See Troubleshooting.

title: WhatsApp rules to know
text: Meta charges per delivered template message, at a rate that depends on the template category and the customer's country. Replies inside the 24-hour window are generally not charged; check Meta's pricing for your region for the current rules. Meta bills these charges to the payment method on your WhatsApp account. WhatFlow's plan charges are separate, and every message Meta accepts counts toward your WhatFlow plan. See Plans and billing.

title: Message templates
text: Every automated WhatsApp message WhatFlow sends is a template: a message written in advance and approved by Meta. You create templates in WhatFlow, WhatFlow submits them to Meta, and each automation sends the template assigned to its trigger event. Templates The page is called Message Templates . You need a connected WhatsApp number to use it. If you are not connected, you see Connect WhatsApp First with a Go to Connections button.

title: Message templates
text: 1. You write the template in the template editor, or start from the template library. 2. You assign a trigger event in Send when , for example Order Confirmation or Abandoned Checkout . This decides which automation can use it. 3. You submit it to Meta. Meta reviews it. This usually takes a few minutes. 4. Once approved, you choose it on the automation page and turn the automation on. When the automation runs, WhatFlow fills the template's variables with the order or customer details and sends it. One active template per event Each trigger event has one active template at a time. If you activate a second template for the same event, it replaces the first one. A template assigned to one event can't be picked for another; it shows "Used by" and the event name. Because only one template is active per event, an automation sends the same template, in the same language, to every customer.

title: Message templates
text: The library has ready-made templates for every event. Open it with Choose From Library or Browse Library . Search by event, category, language or text. For each template: - Customize opens a copy in the editor so you can change it before submitting. - Use As-Is & Submit sends it straight to Meta for review. All library templates are in English (US). If you already have a template with the same name, WhatFlow adds a number to the end, for example wf order confirm req v1 1 . The library includes templates for order confirmation, order notification, order paid, cancellation, fulfillment, every Shipping Journey stage, admin alerts, abandoned checkout, draft orders, back in stock, review requests, Judge.me review requests through Shopify Flow, and broadcasts. Starter templates When you connect WhatsApp, WhatFlow submits a few library templates to Meta for you: order confirmation, order fulfillment, abandoned checkout, a star-rating review request and a Judge.me review request for Flow. They are only submitted. None is activated and no automation is turned on.

title: Message templates
text: Edit Click edit to open the template in the editor. While Meta is reviewing it, the template is read-only. Editing an approved template sends it back to Meta for review. Until Meta approves the change, the template may be unavailable and automations that use it may stop. Assign a backup template before you edit an active one. Shipping Journey keeps its stage assignments, but affected stages can't send until the template is approved again. Duplicate Click duplicate, enter a New Template Name (lowercase letters, numbers and underscores), then choose Duplicate & Submit to Meta or Duplicate & Edit . Delete Click delete and confirm. This can't be undone. The template is also deleted in Meta. If it was the only active template for its event, that automation is turned off.

The automation page explains why, with an Edit message button. When the template is approved again, WhatFlow does not turn the automation back on. Open the automation page and turn it on yourself.

title: Template editor and variables
text: The template editor is where you write a WhatsApp template, choose what fills each variable, add buttons and media, and submit it to Meta. This page covers every field.

title: Template editor and variables
text: - On Templates , click Create My Own , or edit or duplicate a template. - On an automation page, click Create new or Edit in the message card. When you create a template from an automation page, Send when is already set and locked. - From the template library, click Customize . A new template starts with a starter picker. Starters are grouped by category: - Order updates (Utility): "Messages about an order a customer placed." Order confirmation, Order received, Payment received, Shipping update, Out for delivery, Order delivered, Order cancelled, Draft order invoice, New order alert (staff). - Promotions and reminders (Marketing): "Meta charges more for these, and customers must be able to opt out." Abandoned cart reminder, Back in stock, Review request, Promotion. - Verification codes (Authentication): "One-time passcodes. WhatsApp writes the message text." Verification code. You can also start from a blank template. The header has Generate with AI , which opens Shopify Sidekick to draft the template, and Open WhatsApp Manager .

title: Template editor and variables
text: Type the body in Message text . The formatting buttons add WhatsApp formatting: Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, Code, Code block, bullet list, numbered list and quote. Click Insert variable to add a variable such as {{1}} at the cursor. "Variables like {{1}} are filled with order or customer details. Choose them under Personalization." Rules: - The message text is required. - Variables must be numbers: {{1}} , {{2}} and so on. Named variables are not allowed. - "Variables can't be at the start or end of the template." Put some text before the first variable and after the last one. - WhatFlow renumbers variables in the order they appear: header first, then body, then button link. - Shopify Flow Action templates can have at most 7 body variables. Authentication templates If the category is Authentication , WhatsApp writes the message text and you can't edit it. You can choose: Adds that sentence to the message. Shows how long the code is valid. Set Expires in (minutes) from 1 to 90. Default 10. A Copy code button is always included. Authentication templates have no other buttons, header or custom footer.

title: Template editor and variables
text: "Choose what each variable in your message is replaced with when it's sent." For each variable there are two fields: An example value. Meta uses it to review the template. It is never sent to customers. The store field that fills the variable when the message is sent. The list depends on Send when . Choose Custom note attribute… to use an order or checkout attribute instead. Custom note attributes Use this when a value comes from the order's Additional details , for example from a checkout app. "Type the name exactly as it appears under Additional details on the order or checkout." Up to 100 characters. Letter case doesn't matter, and spaces, underscores and hyphens are treated the same. Sent when the order doesn't have that attribute. Up to 200 characters. Custom note attributes are not available for Back in Stock , Customer Broadcast and Shopify Flow Action templates. If a value is empty If a field is empty on the order, WhatFlow sends a blank space in its place. For Order Confirmation , if Shipping Address Line 1 or Shipping City is empty, WhatFlow checks the order again and otherwise sends "Not provided".

title: Order confirmation
text: Order Confirmation sends a WhatsApp message to the customer when a new order is placed, and asks them to confirm or cancel it with a button. Stores use it mostly to check cash on delivery (COD) orders before they pack and ship them. This page covers the settings. For how the Confirm and Cancel buttons tag the order, and how to act on those tags, see COD verification on WhatsApp.

title: Order confirmation
text: 1. A customer places an order in your Shopify store. 2. WhatFlow checks the order against your conditions (payment status or payment method). 3. After the Send delay , WhatFlow sends your active Order Confirmation template to the customer's phone number. 4. WhatFlow tags the order as the message moves through WhatsApp: a "waiting" tag when Meta accepts the message, and your Order tag when WhatsApp reports it delivered or read. 5. The customer taps a button. WhatFlow tags the order with that button's tag and sends the reply you set. 6. If the customer does not answer, WhatFlow can send up to 3 automatic reminders. Turning the automation on does not send messages for orders that were placed before you turned it on. Only new orders are sent.

title: Order confirmation
text: Your WhatsApp number must be connected. See Connect WhatsApp. Home › Order Confirmation The page heading is Order Confirmation . In the message card, click Choose message and pick an approved template, then click Use this message . To write your own, click Create new . See Message templates. When you connect WhatsApp, WhatFlow submits a starter template called Order Confirmation - Detailed to Meta for you. It has Confirm and Cancel buttons. It is not switched on automatically: you still need to choose it here. Under When to send , set the Send delay , and choose a Payment status or Payment methods . For COD stores, pick your cash on delivery method under Payment methods . Under When the customer replies , set what WhatFlow replies and which tag it adds for each button. Click Save . In the Status card, click Turn on . Place a test order using a phone number that is not your connected WhatsApp business number. WhatFlow does not send the confirmation to its own number.

title: COD confirmation
text: With cash on delivery (COD), some customers order and then refuse the parcel. WhatFlow lets you ask every COD customer on WhatsApp to confirm their order before you ship it. You can do this with Confirm and Cancel buttons, or with a one-time code on the Thank you page. This page is about confirming COD orders on WhatsApp. The Cash on Delivery page in the app menu does something else: it adds a COD fee and hides COD at checkout. See COD fee and rules at checkout.

title: COD confirmation
text: Confirm/Cancel buttons One-time code (OTP) Automation Order Confirmation OTP Order Confirmation How the customer confirms Taps a button in a WhatsApp message Enters a 6-digit code on the Thank you page or Order status page Can the customer say no? Yes, with the Cancel button No. They confirm or do nothing. Template category Utility Authentication Set-up guide Order confirmation OTP order confirmation Use one of them for a given order, not both. If both are on for the same orders, the customer is asked twice. Turn one off, or give each one different payment methods. The rest of this page covers the button method.

title: COD confirmation
text: 1. A customer places a COD order. 2. WhatFlow sends your Order Confirmation template with quick-reply buttons, for example Confirm and Cancel . The order gets the tag ⚠ Confirmation Pending once the message is delivered. 3. The customer taps a button. 4. WhatFlow removes the pending tag, adds that button's tag to the order, and sends the reply you set for that button. With the default settings: Customer taps Tag added Reply sent First button (Confirm) ✅ Order Confirmed Thank you for the confirmation! Your order will be at your doorstep soon! Second button (Cancel) ❌ Order Canceled Your order has been cancelled. You may confirm again if this was a mistake. You can change every reply and tag. See Order confirmation settings. Tapping Cancel does not cancel the order in Shopify. WhatFlow only adds the ❌ Order Canceled tag and sends the reply. The order stays open, and the stock is not restocked. You must cancel the order yourself, or set up Shopify Flow to do it (see Act on the tags). The default reply to Cancel says "Your order has been cancelled". If you do not cancel these orders, change the reply to something like "We received your cancellation request."

title: COD confirmation
text: Home › Order Confirmation Click Choose message and pick an approved template that has quick-reply buttons. The Order Confirmation - Detailed starter has Confirm and Cancel buttons. Under When to send , open Payment methods and pick your cash on delivery method. Now prepaid orders do not get the message. Under When the customer replies , check Reply with and Tag the order for each button. Give each button its own tag. You need these tags to filter orders and to use automatic reminders. Click Save , then click Turn on in the Status card.

title: COD confirmation
text: Dear Sara , Thank you for your order. This is a confirmation message. Order Number: 1001 Total: 49.99 USD Please confirm your order ASAP. After the customer taps Confirm : Thank you for the confirmation! Your order will be at your doorstep soon! Tapping a button sends a message to your business, so it opens a 24-hour window. The reply and the tap also show in Live Inbox, where your team can follow up with free-form messages.

title: COD confirmation
text: - 3-day limit. A button tap counts only within 3 days of the confirmation message. Taps after that do not add a tag or send a reply. - Changing the answer. If the customer taps Cancel and later taps Confirm (within 3 days), the new tag replaces the old one. - Typed replies. If the customer types the button text as a reply to the message instead of tapping, WhatFlow treats it like a tap. Matching ignores upper and lower case. - No double replies. A button tap never also triggers a general auto-reply. - Only quick-reply buttons count. Link and phone buttons do not add tags or send replies.

title: COD confirmation
text: WhatFlow tags orders. What happens next is up to you. Filter orders by tag In Shopify admin, go to Orders and filter by tag: - ✅ Order Confirmed : ready to pack and ship. - ❌ Order Canceled : cancel the order in Shopify, or call the customer. - ⚠ Confirmation Pending : the customer got the message but has not answered. - ⏳ ⚠ Confirmation Pending : the message was sent but not delivered yet. - A tag starting with WhatsApp: : the message failed. See the failure tags. You can save each filter as a view in Shopify so your team can open it quickly. Use Shopify Flow WhatFlow adds a Shopify Flow trigger called WhatsApp Order Reply . It starts when a customer replies on WhatsApp, with a button or with text, to a message about one of their orders. It gives Flow the order, the customer, the reply type, the button text, the button payload, the message text and the sender's phone number. You can use it to cancel the order, add a note, or alert your team when a customer taps Cancel. See Shopify Flow.

title: COD fees and checkout rules
text: The Cash on Delivery page lets you charge a fee for cash on delivery (COD) and hide COD at checkout for some orders, for example very large carts or certain countries. It works through a Shopify payment customization called WhatFlow COD Checkout . This page does not send WhatsApp messages. To ask COD customers to confirm their order on WhatsApp, see COD verification on WhatsApp. Cash on Delivery (in the app menu)

title: COD fees and checkout rules
text: Shopify payment customizations run in supported online checkouts. They do not run in Point of Sale, and Shop Pay supports limited payment-method changes. Test your fee and rules in your store checkout before you take live orders.

title: COD fees and checkout rules
text: Shopify has no built-in fee for a payment method. WhatFlow adds the fee as a shipping rate instead: 1. You create a shipping rate priced at your fee, for example "Cash on Delivery fee". 2. You link that rate to COD in WhatFlow. 3. At checkout, while the fee is Active : - COD is shown only when the customer has selected a linked COD shipping rate (in every delivery group of the order). - When a COD shipping rate is selected, all other payment methods are hidden. So a customer who wants to pay with cash on delivery must pick the COD rate and pay its price. A customer who wants to pay online picks a normal rate. The fee cannot be skipped.

title: COD fees and checkout rules
text: The page shows four steps under How WhatFlow COD works . In Shopify, go to Settings › Payments › Manual payment methods and add Cash on Delivery (COD) . Click Configure method to open it. The badge shows Active in Shopify when it is set up, or Needs setup . In Shopify, go to Settings › Shipping and delivery . In each zone where you offer COD, add a rate priced at your fee, for example "Cash on Delivery fee". Click Open shipping settings to go there. Click Link rates , select your COD shipping rates, set Fee status to Active — apply fee in checkout , and save. The badge shows Linked & active , Draft or Not linked . Click Open storefront and place a test order. Check that COD appears only with the COD rate, and that the fee is added.

title: COD fees and checkout rules
text: The Preferences section has three items: - Manual payment method : which payment method WhatFlow treats as COD. - Cash on Delivery fee : the fee status and how many shipping rates are linked. - COD limits & restrictions : rules that hide COD. Manual payment method Pick the name of your COD payment method from the list Shopify returns. If yours is not listed, choose Other / enter custom name and type it in Exact checkout payment method name , exactly as customers see it at checkout. From here you can click Continue to fee or Set up limits instead . If you use both the fee and limits, they must use the same payment method name. Cash on Delivery fee - Active — apply fee in checkout : enforces the COD shipping rate in supported checkouts. - Draft — save without activating : saves your settings, no fee at checkout. - Inactive — disabled : no fee at checkout. Pick the COD rates from your Shopify shipping rates, or choose + Enter custom rate name... and type it in Custom shipping rate name . Up to 50 rate names, 150 characters each. How WhatFlow compares the rate name at checkout with your rate names: Exact , Contains or Starts with . You must select at least one priced COD shipping rate

title: COD fees and checkout rules
text: On Limit Cash on Delivery , you set rules. When an order matches any active rule, Cash on Delivery is hidden from the customer at checkout. Active enforces the limits in checkout. Draft and Inactive do not. The COD payment method these rules hide. Each rule is a checkbox. Tick it to show its field. Rules that work at checkout Rule What it does Maximum value Hides COD when the cart total is above this amount, in your store currency. Minimum value Hides COD when the cart total is below this amount. The minimum can't be higher than the maximum. Limit if any product is in cart Hides COD when the cart contains any product you pick. Limit if country is / is not Uses 2-letter country codes, for example US, CA, IN. Limit if state/province is / is not Uses Shopify's province codes, for example CA or NJ, not the full name. Limit if city is / is not Matches when the city contains the text you enter. Limit if postal/pin code is / is not Uses the postal or PIN code of the address. Limit if any discount is applied Hides COD when the order has a discount. Shipping rate restrictions (optional) Allows COD only with the shipping rates you choose. text: COD doesn't show at checkout at all - If the fee is Active , COD only appears after the customer picks a linked COD shipping rate. title: OTP verification
text: OTP order confirmation lets customers confirm their order with a 6-digit code sent to their WhatsApp. They enter the code on the Thank you page right after checkout, or later on the Order status page. When the code is right, WhatFlow tags the order as confirmed. Stores use it to verify cash on delivery (COD) orders. Home › OTP Order Confirmation The page heading is OTP order confirmation .

title: OTP verification
text: 1. The customer places an order. If the order matches your conditions, a Confirm your order block shows on the Thank you page. 2. The customer enters their WhatsApp number and taps Send code on WhatsApp . The order gets the tag ⏳ Awaiting WhatsApp OTP . 3. WhatFlow sends your code message on WhatsApp. 4. The customer enters the code and taps Confirm order . 5. WhatFlow removes the waiting tag and adds ✓ WhatsApp Verified . 6. If you set one, WhatFlow sends a follow-up message, like a thank-you. Customers who leave without confirming can come back to the Order status page, which shows whether the order is confirmed, or lets them confirm it. Compared with Confirm/Cancel buttons Order Confirmation sends a WhatsApp message with buttons, and the customer can also tap Cancel. OTP only lets the customer confirm. See COD verification on WhatsApp for a comparison. If Order Confirmation is also on, the same customers also get its confirm or cancel message. Turn one off, or give each one different payment methods.

title: OTP verification
text: The code message must be an approved template in the Authentication category. WhatsApp writes the text of these messages for you. You can only choose to add a security line ("For your security, do not share this code.") and an expiry time. A Copy code button is always included. See Template editor. On the OTP order confirmation page, under Message , choose your approved authentication template. Only authentication messages work here. Under Where customers confirm : - Thank you page : click Add to Thank you page . This opens the checkout editor. Works on every plan, and you can move the block anywhere on the page. - Order status page : click Add to Order status page . Save in the editor. Each block shows Added or Not added . Under Which orders , set Payment status or Payment methods . Other orders never see the block. Click Save , then click Turn on in the Status card. You can't turn it on until you choose an approved code message.

title: OTP verification
text: Which orders Any order , Unpaid orders only (e.g. cash on delivery) or Paid orders only . Pick your cash on delivery method to ask only those customers. Leave it empty for every method. Order tags Added when the customer asks for a code, and removed once they confirm. Up to 40 characters. Added when the customer enters the right code. Up to 40 characters. After confirmation Optional. Choose a Utility or Marketing template to send to the number that received the code, like a thank-you or "your order is confirmed" message. Click Remove to stop sending it.

title: OTP verification
text: On the Thank you page, the block shows: - the heading Confirm your order , - the text "We'll send a 6-digit code to your WhatsApp. Enter it here to confirm your order.", - a WhatsApp number field and a Send code on WhatsApp button. After the code is sent, the customer sees Enter 6-digit code , a Confirm order button, a Resend code option (with a countdown), and Use a different number . When the code is right, the block shows Order confirmed and "Thank you! Your order is confirmed." The block is translated into Arabic, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Dutch, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish and Turkish. You can change every text in the block settings in the checkout editor, for example the heading, the button labels and the success message.

title: OTP verification
text: Limit Value Code length 6 digits Code expiry The expiry set on your template (default 10 minutes, 1 to 90) Wait before resending 60 seconds Codes per phone number 3 every 10 minutes Wrong codes After 5 wrong codes, the customer must wait 15 minutes Codes per store 300 per hour - If the order has phone numbers on it, the number the customer enters must match one of them. - The code message is never blocked by the Blocklist. - Every code needs an active WhatFlow plan. Without one, no code is sent. - If Meta restricts your WhatsApp number, WhatFlow turns off all automations. Turn them back on yourself after Meta lifts the restriction.

text: The block doesn't show on the Thank you page - Check that the block shows Added on the OTP page. If not, add it in the checkout editor and save. - Check Payment status and Payment methods . Orders that don't match never see the block. - Check that the automation is on. Customers get two confirmation requests Order Confirmation is also on for the same orders. Turn one off, or set different payment methods for each.

title: Paid, cancelled and other order messages

title: Paid, cancelled and other order messages
text: Home › Order Notification Sends a simple message when an order is placed, without asking the customer to confirm. Use it as a WhatsApp version of the order confirmation email. If both Order Notification and Order Confirmation are on, the customer gets both messages. To split them, use Payment methods : for example, Order Confirmation for your COD method, and Order Notification for the others.

title: Paid, cancelled and other order messages
text: Home › Order Paid Sends a message when Shopify marks an order as paid. This page has Fulfillment status instead of Payment status . For cash on delivery orders, payment is often marked after the parcel is delivered. If you set Fulfillment status to Partially fulfilled orders only or Fulfilled orders only , WhatFlow can also send the message when an already-paid order becomes fulfilled and matches that status.

title: Paid, cancelled and other order messages
text: Home › Order Fulfillment Sends a message when the whole order is fulfilled. The message can include tracking details from the latest fulfillment that has tracking: Tracking Number , Tracking URL and Shipping Carrier . Shopify only reports an order as fulfilled when every item is fulfilled. Partial shipments do not trigger this message. To message customers for each shipment and each carrier scan, use Shipping updates.

title: Paid, cancelled and other order messages
text: Home › Order Cancellation Sends a message when an order is cancelled in Shopify. Besides the usual order fields, the template can use: - Cancel Reason : Shopify's reason code, for example "customer". - Cancelled At : the date and time of the cancellation. Products x Quantity shows the quantities that were ordered, not the quantities left after the cancellation.

title: Paid, cancelled and other order messages
text: Home › Admin Notification Sends a message to your own team for each new order, so staff hear about orders on WhatsApp. WhatsApp numbers that get a message for each new order. Include the country code, like +14155550123. Click Add number to add more. You need at least one number before you can turn it on. - The alert is sent even if the customer has no phone number. - Each team number gets its own template message, and each one is billed. - These are template messages, so your team doesn't need to have messaged you first. - If a team number is on your Blocklist and the blocklist covers order updates, that number is skipped.

title: Paid, cancelled and other order messages
text: All these automations can use the common order fields: Shop Name, Shop Website URL, Order Name ( 1001), Order Number, Total Price, Subtotal Price, Total Tax, Currency, Payment Status, Payment Method / Gateway, Delivery Method, Financial Status (raw), Fulfillment Status, Order Status URL, Order Date, Order Note, Products x Quantity, Variant x Quantity, Products x Price, Shipping Fees, customer name, email and phone, and the shipping and billing address fields. Extra fields: - Order Fulfillment : Tracking Number, Tracking URL, Shipping Carrier, Shipment Status, Estimated Delivery. - Order Cancellation : Cancel Reason, Cancelled At. See Template editor.

title: Paid, cancelled and other order messages
text: - Subscription required. Every automated message needs an active WhatFlow plan. Without one, the message is skipped and the order is tagged WhatFlow: Subscription Required . See Plans and billing. - Meta restrictions turn automations off. If Meta restricts your WhatsApp number, WhatFlow turns off every automation. After Meta lifts the restriction, turn each one back on yourself. - Template problems turn it off. If Meta pauses, disables or rejects the template, or rates it low quality, and there's no other usable template, the automation turns off. Turn it on again after you fix or replace the template. - Phone number. WhatFlow uses the billing phone, then shipping phone, order phone and customer phone. Orders with no valid phone number are skipped (except for Admin Notification).

title: Paid, cancelled and other order messages
text: Problem Fix Turn on doesn't work Choose an approved template. Wait if it says it's waiting for Meta's review. For Admin Notification, add at least one team number. "Use international format with country code, for example +14155550123." Enter the team number with + and the country code, 7 to 15 digits. Order Fulfillment didn't send The order was only partly fulfilled. Use Shipping updates for partial shipments. Unpaid orders are not sent Partially paid and authorized orders are not "unpaid". Use Any order , or pick payment methods instead. Order tagged WhatFlow: Subscription Required Choose a plan in Billing . Order has a WhatsApp: failure tag See Failure tags.

title: Shipping updates
text: Shipping Journey sends the customer a WhatsApp message at each step of delivery: when the label is bought, when the carrier picks up the package, when it is out for delivery, when it is delivered, and more. You choose which steps send a message, and which template each step uses. Home › Shipping Journey The page heading is Shipping journey .

title: Shipping updates
text: When your carrier scans a package, Shopify records a tracking event on the fulfillment. WhatFlow receives that event, reads the order again, finds the matching shipment, and sends the template you set for that step. - One message per step per shipment. If the same event comes twice, the customer gets one message. - Each shipment of an order is handled on its own, so partial shipments work. - These messages depend on tracking events from Shopify. If your carrier or shipping app does not report a step to Shopify, that step's message is not sent. Shipping Journey is different from Order Fulfillment , which sends one message when the whole order is fulfilled. See Order updates.

title: Shipping updates

title: Shipping updates
text: - Editing a template. Editing an approved template sends it back to Meta for review. Steps that use it can't send until it is approved again. Assign a backup template first if you need to edit one. - Subscription required. Every automated message needs an active WhatFlow plan. Without one, the message is skipped and the order is tagged WhatFlow: Subscription Required . - Meta restrictions turn automations off. If Meta restricts your WhatsApp number, WhatFlow turns off Shipping Journey and all other automations. Turn them back on yourself after Meta lifts the restriction. - Old events. Events older than 30 days are not sent. - Review requests. Review requests set to After delivery use the same "delivered" event from your carrier.

title: Shipping updates
text: A step never sends - Check the step's badge. It must be Active . - Your carrier may not report that step to Shopify. Open the order in Shopify and check the tracking events on the fulfillment. If the event is not there, WhatFlow can't send a message for it. - Check that the order has a valid phone number. I can't turn on Shipping Journey You see "Turn on at least one shipping update and assign it a template, then save before enabling." Turn on a step, choose an approved template, save, then turn on. The customer got no message and the order has a failure tag See Failure tags.

title: Review requests
text: Review requests ask customers for a product review on WhatsApp a few days after their order is delivered, fulfilled, paid or placed. Each order is asked only once. Home › Review Requests The page heading is Review requests .

title: Review requests
text: 1. An order event happens: delivery, fulfillment, payment or order creation, depending on your setting. 2. WhatFlow schedules the request for after your wait time. If that time falls outside your sending hours, it waits until the window opens. 3. Right before sending, WhatFlow checks the order again. It skips the order if it was cancelled, refunded or returned, or if it has a tag you excluded. 4. WhatFlow sends your review template. The order gets the tag ⭐ Review Requested . 5. If the template has quick-reply buttons (for example star ratings), WhatFlow can reply and tag the order when the customer taps one. The reviewed product is the most expensive item still on the order.

title: Review requests
text: In the message card, choose an approved template. The Template Library has several review templates, for example Review Request - Star Rating and Review Request - Store Review (Google) . To send customers to a review page, add a link button to the message. Under When to ask , choose the trigger and the wait time. If your template has quick-reply buttons, set a reply and a tag for each one under When the customer replies . Click Save , then Turn on in the Status card.

title: Review requests
text: When to ask - After delivery : counted from the carrier's "delivered" event. You can use fulfillment as a fallback when no delivery is reported. - After fulfillment : counted from when the order is fully fulfilled. - After payment : counted from when the order is marked paid. For cash on delivery this is usually the delivery day. - After order is placed : counted from when the order is created. How long to wait after the event, in Days or Hours . 0 sends as soon as possible, within your sending window. Up to 30 days (720 hours). Shown for After delivery only. If no delivery is reported, send after fulfillment instead. Turn it off to wait for a reported delivery. Used for the fallback. At least 1 hour, up to 30 days. If a delivery event arrives later, the request moves to the delivery-based time. Set From and Until in your store's time zone. Requests that fall due outside these hours wait until the window opens. The start and end can't be the same hour. If you change Send the review request to a different trigger, requests that were already scheduled are cancelled. text: The bottom of the page lists the last 100 requests, with the order, status ( scheduled , sent or skipped ), trigger, time and details. When a request is skipped, Details shows why: Reason Meaning Review requests were turned off The automation was off when the request was due. Fulfillment fallback was turned off The request was waiting on the fallback, which you turned off. The trigger was changed after this was scheduled You changed Send the review request . Already asked for a review Each order is asked once. Order has an excluded tag It has a tag from Skip orders with these tags . Order is not fulfilled The order was not fulfilled. No product to review WhatFlow found no product on the order to ask about. No phone number The order has no phone number. Rescheduled for after delivery A delivery event arrived, so the request moved to the delivery-based time.

title: Review requests
text: If you use Judge.me, the page links to WhatFlow's Shopify Flow templates for sending Judge.me review requests instead. The Template Library also has Judge.me review templates for use with Shopify Flow. See Shopify Flow.

title: Review requests
text: - Subscription required. Every automated message needs an active WhatFlow plan. Without one, the message is skipped and the order is tagged WhatFlow: Subscription Required . - Meta restrictions turn automations off. If Meta restricts your WhatsApp number, WhatFlow turns off review requests and all other automations. Turn them back on yourself after Meta lifts the restriction. - After delivery needs carrier events. If your carrier does not report deliveries to Shopify, keep Use fulfillment as a fallback on.

title: Review requests
text: I can't turn it on The page tells you what is missing: "Choose a WhatsApp template.", "The template must be approved by Meta.", or "The template has a RED quality rating." Also check that From and Until are not the same hour. A request was not sent Check Recent review requests for the order. The Details column shows the skip reason. The customer tapped a rating but no tag was added The tap came more than 14 days after the request, or that button has no tag set.

title: Back in stock alerts
text: Back in Stock lets customers ask for a WhatsApp alert on a product that is sold out. When the product variant is restocked, WhatFlow messages everyone who asked. Home › Back in Stock The page heading is Back in stock .

title: Back in stock alerts
text: 1. You add the Stock Notification block to your product page. 2. On an out-of-stock variant, the customer taps Notify me when back in stock , enters their name and phone number, and taps Submit request . 3. The request shows on the Back in stock page as Pending . 4. When Shopify reports that the variant is back in stock, WhatFlow sends your Back in Stock template to every pending request for that variant. It reads the product again, so the name, price, image and link are current. 5. The request changes to Notified . Restocks while the automation is off are not notified later. WhatFlow keeps collecting requests while Back in Stock is turned off, but if a product is restocked during that time, nobody is messaged, and turning it on afterwards does not send them. Turn Back in Stock on before you restock.

title: Back in stock alerts
text: Under Product page button , click Add to product page . This opens the theme editor with the Stock Notification block. Save the theme. In the theme editor, open the block settings and change Default Country Code Prefix . The default is +57 (Colombia). Set it to your own country, for example +44 or +91, and change Phone Input Placeholder to match. In the message card, choose an approved Back in Stock template. The Template Library has Back In Stock - Standard and Back In Stock - Available Now . In the Status card, click Turn on . Filter by All statuses , Pending , Notified or Failed .
